title: F-CLASS COMPRESSOR MECHNICALLY-ATTACHED SHROUD S17 INSPECTION
reason_for_revision: This revision is intended to communicate the availability of new configuration Gen-V S17 assembly and availability to modify earlier mechanically-attached shroud S17 generations to Gen-V S17 in GE designated service shop.
purpose: This TIL advises operators to monitor the mechanically-attached shroud compressor S17 configurations and provides recommendations for mitigating any observed distress.
compliance_category_text: Maintenance - Identifies maintenance guidelines or best practices for reliable equipment operation.
scope_of_work: Manpower if replacement of S17 segment is required (these support personnel will already be onsite during MI): Two GE field technicians; One GE Field TA.
service_recommendation_line_items: When S17s are NOT exposed: perform an annual borescope per GER 3620; also perform borescope inspection during scheduled outages such as planned Combustion Inspections (CI) or Hot Gas Path Inspections (HGPI) when the CDC is not removed.
During all borescope inspections: inspect 100% of the shrouded S17 for signs of distress (inspect along the vane towards the bushing area, shroud holes, and between vane tips and the shroud).

When S17s are exposed (Major Inspection (MI) or if the CDC is removed during a Hot Gas Path Inspection (HGPI)): visually inspect for bushing wear, tenon damage, shroud hole ovalization, and wear between the vane tips and the shroud; remove or borescope-inspect S17s in the lower half.

If significant distress, cracks, detached bushings, or ovalized shroud hole are found during Inspection Procedure 1 or 2: document with pictures and submit to your GE Services representative for engineering disposition.

If wear or damage is observed: order and install the latest Gen-V S17 configuration as a set for durability improvement; it is acceptable to replace only the damaged segment with the latest S17 segment (Gen-V configuration).

If desired: use GE refurbishment services to modify earlier mechanically-attached shroud S17 configurations to the latest Gen-V configuration based on approved repair instruction (consult service representative).
completion_criteria_text: This TIL can be marked completed when the latest Gen-V S17 configuration has been installed across the entire stage.
maintenance_trigger_text: Annual borescope inspection; borescope during scheduled outages such as planned CI or HGPI when the CDC is not removed; visual inspection when S17s are exposed during MI or when CDC is removed during HGPI.
recommended_interval_or_trigger: Annual borescope is recommended per GER 3620 (when S17s are NOT exposed).

Borescope inspection during scheduled outages such as planned Combustion Inspections (CI) or Hot Gas Path Inspections (HGPI), when the CDC is not removed; visual inspection when S17s are exposed during Major Inspection (MI) or if the CDC is removed during a Hot Gas Path Inspection (HGPI).
frame_or_model_applicability_text: All 7F.03, 7F.04, 7FB, and 9F.05 (9FB) units with mechanically-attached shroud S17 segments.
hardware_or_part_configuration_text: Mechanically-attached shroud compressor S17 configurations including welded bolt configuration (bolt secured via one or two tack welds), staked bolt configuration (stake bolt 180° apart), staked bolt configuration with changed bushing material (2016 Gen-IV), and Gen-V S17 assembly with both bushing and shroud made of the same cobalt-chromium based alloy. Recommendations apply for Gen-IV and earlier mechanically-attached shroud configurations with and without compressor discharge casing (CDC) removal. All configurations of S17 shrouded segments are compatible and therefore individual segments may be replaced with the newer configuration.
prerequisite_outage_or_inspection_contex: Inspection Procedure 1 applies when S17s are NOT exposed (CDC not removed). Inspection Procedure 2 applies when S17s are exposed (Major Inspection (MI) or if the CDC is removed during a Hot Gas Path Inspection (HGPI)).
sbom_trigger_reason: Document requires verification/installation of a specific configuration revision (Gen-V S17 assembly) and discusses multiple S17 generations (Gen-IV and earlier) with configuration-dependent inspection and replacement guidance.

parts_referenced.context: Gen-V S17 assembly / latest Gen-V S17 configuration (S17 shrouded segments) recommended for installation across the entire stage; acceptable to replace only damaged segment with Gen-V segment.
Mechanically-attached shroud S17 hardware elements referenced in distress/inspection: bolts (welded bolt or staked bolt), bushings, shroud, tenon, shroud holes.

reference_documents.context: Referenced as recommending installing counterbore plugs and modifying the control system to reduce aft end distress.

configuration_variables: S17 mechanically-attached shroud configuration generation (Gen-IV and earlier vs Gen-V)
Bolt retention method (welded bolt vs staked bolt)
Whether S17s are exposed / whether CDC is removed (CDC removed vs not removed)
configuration_summary: Inspection method and access depend on whether S17s are exposed (CDC removed) and on S17 mechanically-attached shroud generation/configuration; Gen-V S17 assembly is the recommended durability upgrade and is compatible with earlier S17 shrouded segments for segment-level replacement.
severity_signals: wear between the vane tips and the shroud
damage to the bolts, shrouds, and/or bushings
failure_consequences: Excessive wear between the vane and bushing may cause S17 tip to detach from the shroud, and the S17 will act as a cantilever, increasing the stress on the vane.
Over time, this condition poses a risk, possibly resulting in secondary damages to the adjacent airfoils and possible migration forward into the R17 wheel.
risk_summary: Observed distress/wear in mechanically-attached shrouded S17 configurations can progress to tip detachment and increased vane stress, with potential secondary damage to adjacent airfoils and possible migration forward into the R17 wheel.

source_snippets.snippet: All 7F.03, 7F.04, 7FB, and 9F.05 (9FB) units with mechanically-attached shroud S17 segments.
An annual borescope is recommended per GER 3620.
During all borescope inspections, it is recommended to inspect 100% of the shrouded S17 for signs of distress.
It is recommended to visually inspect for any signs of bushing wear (Figure 8), tenon damage, shroud hole ovalization (Figure 9), and wear between the vane tips and the shroud.

If significant distress, cracks, detached bushings, or ovalized shroud hole are found during Inspection Procedure 1 or 2, the damage must be documented with pictures and submitted to your GE Services representative for engineering disposition.
If wear or damage is observed during the inspection above, it is recommended to order and install the latest Gen-V S17 configuration as a set for durability improvement.
This TIL can be marked completed when the latest Gen-V S17 configuration has been installed across the entire stage.

Excessive wear between the vane and bushing may cause S17 tip to detach from the shroud, and the S17 will act as a cantilever, increasing the stress on the vane. Over time, this condition poses a risk, possibly resulting in secondary damages to the adjacent airfoils and possible migration forward into the R17 wheel.
